candidates.rationale: The current writer serializes before opening, but open(..., "w") truncates the live destination and writes in place. A crash or short/failed write can leave corrupt JSON; project, ghosts and system are also separate commits. This is a durability defect in the directly callable consolidation API, not proof that corruption occurred on this host.

source_checks.observation: Payload JSON validation occurs before an in-place truncating write; no temporary file, atomic replacement or fsync.
Project read/modify/write is the first independent update.
Ghosts and system are read and written independently after project persistence.

guards: Pre-serialization catches invalid JSON before truncation but does not make the write crash-safe.
Topology existence check and SIGKILL on error provide no rollback.

candidates.rationale: The persistent SQLite deadline stores time.monotonic()+delay and is compared against a later boot/process clock with no boot identity or rebasing. A reboot that restarts the monotonic epoch can defer old retries by the previous uptime, or otherwise alter the intended delay. Persistence of the raw monotonic reading does not create a durable clock.

source_checks.observation: The consumer compares persisted next_retry_at with time.monotonic().

The producer persists REAL next_retry_at and computes it from time.monotonic().

guards: Both producer and consumer use the same clock within a boot.
No boot marker, recovery rebasing or durable wall-clock conversion is present.
